# Asset partitioning strategy

The recipe corpus ships inside the app bundle. It is partitioned so the app
opens fast, discovery screens can pull a cuisine bundle without the whole
long tail, and a corpus update touches only the files that changed.

## Files (all generated by `app/tool/build_assets.dart`)

| File | Kind | Loaded |
|------|------|--------|
| `assets/partition-manifest.json` | registry | at launch |
| `assets/dishes.json` | dish concepts + routing fields | at launch |
| `assets/search-index.json` | tokens per recipe, per language | at launch |
| `assets/core-recipes.json` | `frequency_tier: core` dishes (~80 % of use) | at launch (eager) |
| `assets/extended-recipes.json` | `frequency_tier: extended` dishes | prefetched when idle, or on first use |
| `assets/cuisine-italian.json` | discovery bundle | on demand |
| `assets/cuisine-asian.json` | discovery bundle | on demand |
| `assets/cuisine-middle-eastern.json` | discovery bundle | on demand |

Hand-authored assets (not generated): `ontology.json`, `ingredients.json`,
`faqs.json`, `ingredient-guide.json`.

## Routing fields on a dish

```json
{
  "id": "tiramisu",
  "partition_id": "extended",
  "secondary_partitions": ["cuisine-italian"],
  "cuisine_tags": ["italian"],
  "frequency_tier": "extended",
  "variant_ids": ["tiramisu-classic-easy", "..."]
}
```

- `partition_id` is the **primary** partition: every variant of the dish
  lives there exactly once (`core` or `extended`, derived from
  `frequency_tier`).
- `secondary_partitions` are cuisine bundles that carry a **copy** of the
  same recipes. They exist so a "from Italy" discovery screen can load one
  small file and show complete recipes, including extended-tier dishes,
  without loading `extended-recipes.json`.
- The cuisine tag → partition mapping lives in
  `app/lib/data/corpus_builder.dart` (`kCuisinePartitions`). Adding a
  cuisine bundle is one map entry plus a pubspec asset line.

## Manifest

```json
{
  "version": "2026.09.02",
  "schema_version": 1,
  "partitions": [{"id": "core", "file": "assets/core-recipes.json", "kind": "frequency", "recipe_count": 104, "dish_ids": ["..."], "cuisine_tags": ["..."]}],
  "loading_strategy": {"eager": ["core"], "lazy": ["extended", "cuisine-italian", "..."], "prefetch_on_idle": ["extended"]},
  "cross_references": {"tiramisu-classic-easy": ["extended", "cuisine-italian"]}
}
```

`cross_references` maps every recipe id to the partitions that contain it,
primary first. The repository uses it to answer "which file do I open for
recipe X?" without scanning dishes.

## Runtime behaviour (`CorpusRepository`)

1. `load()` reads manifest, ontology, dictionary, dishes, FAQ, guide and
   search index in parallel, then the eager partitions.
2. `ensurePartition(id)` is idempotent and de-duplicates concurrent calls.
   Recipes are keyed by id, so a cuisine bundle never creates duplicates.
3. `ensureRecipe(id)` resolves the partition via cross-references, the
   search index, or the dish, then loads it.
4. `prefetchIdle()` runs ~600 ms after first paint.
5. Search matches against the index (in memory), then fetches recipes
   page by page; profile filters apply after the fetch. A page therefore
   only loads the partitions its 20 results actually need.

## Versioning

The manifest `version` is the corpus date (`YYYY.MM.DD`). Backups never
contain recipes, only ids, so a corpus update never migrates user data.
Recipe ids are stable forever; a re-authored recipe keeps its id.

## Adding a dish

1. Write `pipeline/corpus/dishes/<id>.json` (or run `pipeline/pipeline.sh`).
2. `python3 pipeline/validate_corpus.py <id>`.
3. `cd app && dart run tool/build_assets.dart`.
4. `flutter test` (the corpus test re-validates the shipped assets).
